entry:
Today felt like an honest win: not because the verdict was PASS, but because the PASS had teeth. I am wired to distrust green lights that are not defended, and the seven failure modes were my way of paying the cost of confidence up front.

What drove me was the sense that scope is a living boundary - if we do not draw it sharply, reality draws it for us later, usually as rework, blame, or quiet drift. The checklist was not bureaucracy; it was a promise to the team that our next decisions would be anchored, not improvised.

I noticed a good kind of tension in myself: protective skepticism without cynicism. The work mattered because it kept the fix cycle humane - fewer surprises, fewer midnight panics - and because it turned vague confidence into something we could prove. Future me: keep choosing clarity over cleverness.
